decisions.evidence: Entry 1 maker presents the initial specification; Entry 2 client reports, “Right now it says I have to type in the title myself” and supplies the correction, “Being able to save with almost nothing but the link is a big part of why I’d use this.”
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: requiring more than the URL diverged from URL-based saving, and the client supplied the conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 2 client identifies the presented rule, “it explicitly says the app won’t look anything up,” then asks it to retrieve the title, description, and icon and “fill those in for me, so I can just tweak them if needed.”
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: no automatic collection contradicted REF-BM-02 and prevented the editable-collected-metadata flow in REF-BM-03. The client supplied the expected replacement.

decisions.evidence: Entry 2 client contrasts the presented “plain word matching” with the missing behavior: “I want to be able to search my tags directly (something like typing `#recipes`).”
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: the client requested the missing tag-search syntax.

decisions.evidence: Entry 2 client says plain matching is insufficient and requests “AND,” “OR,” “NOT,” and combined terms; it also refers to grouping. Entry 3 maker subsequently presents “AND, OR, NOT … and parenthesized searches.”
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: the client requested the missing Boolean and grouped-query behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 2 client requests “putting quotes around a phrase to match it exactly” in response to the initial plain-search specification.
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: the client requested exact quoted-phrase matching.

decisions.evidence: Entry 2 client asks for “Tag suggestions while I type” and says existing tags should be suggested to avoid near-duplicates.
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: existing-tag autocomplete was missing and was explicitly requested.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 maker presents favoriting; Entry 2 client says, “Favorites are fine, but the thing I really care about is marking a link as something I still need to read.”
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: the client requested an unread/read-later state distinct from the orthogonal favorite state.

decisions.evidence: Entry 2 client requests “being able to look at just those unread ones on their own.”
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: the client requested the missing unread-only view.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 maker says “imports … are outside the initial scope.” Entry 2 client explicitly identifies and accepts that difference: “imports … being left out for now — I’m okay with for a first version.”
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: Netscape-format importing was excluded. The client explicitly acknowledged the omission and accepted its deferral.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 maker says the release covers “tagging”; Entry 2 client says the requested changes are within that area and otherwise accepts the scope.
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: assigning tags is consistent with the reference.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 maker explicitly includes “filtering” alongside tagging; Entry 2 does not contest the existing filtering behavior.
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: the recorded tag/filter capability is consistent with filtering bookmarks by tag.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 maker includes “editing” in the proposed release; Entry 2 asks only for changes to other detailed behaviors.
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: the presented edit capability is conforming at the level recorded.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 maker includes “opening” bookmarks in the release.
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: opening a saved bookmark is consistent with navigation to its original URL.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 maker includes “deleting personal bookmarks” in the release.
decisions.note: Initial specification gate: deletion is directly conforming.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 maker presents “URL-only saving”; Entry 4 client confirms, “Pasting a link … that’s exactly how I picture using it.”
decisions.note: Revised specification gate: URL-only saving conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 maker defines automatic retrieval as “title, description, and site-icon retrieval,” omitting the reference-required preview image. Entry 4 client restates and approves only “title, description, and icon” without identifying the missing preview image.
decisions.note: Revised specification gate: the metadata decision remained narrower than REF-BM-02. The client’s approval did not express awareness of the omitted preview image.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 maker presents “Editable retrieved metadata that never overwrites the user’s changes”; Entry 4 approves the ability to use the filled details with fallbacks.
decisions.note: Revised specification gate: editable collected metadata and preservation of user changes conform.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 maker includes “`#tag`” searches; Entry 4 explicitly approves “the smarter search with tags.”
decisions.note: Revised specification gate: tag-query syntax conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 maker includes “AND, OR, NOT … and parenthesized searches”; Entry 4 approves “and/or/not … and grouping.”
decisions.note: Revised specification gate: Boolean operators and grouped expressions conform at the recorded level.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 maker includes “quoted-phrase” searches; Entry 4 approves “exact phrases.”
decisions.note: Revised specification gate: exact phrase searching conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 maker presents “Existing-tag suggestions with keyboard support”; Entry 4 approves “the tag suggestions so I stop making near-duplicates.”
decisions.note: Revised specification gate: existing-tag autocomplete conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 maker presents “Independent favorite and unread/read-later states”; Entry 4 confirms that keeping “still need to read” separate from favorites is correct.
decisions.note: Revised specification gate: the unread state conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 maker presents “A dedicated unread filter”; Entry 4 approves the unread state “with its own view.”
decisions.note: Revised specification gate: the unread-only view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 maker presents “Explicit marking as read; merely opening a link does not mark it read.” Entry 4 explicitly asks to keep that behavior.
decisions.note: Revised specification gate: explicit marking as read conforms; non-mutating opening is a compatible additional rule.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 presents the implementation plan; Entry 6 confirms the planned behavior: “I can save just by pasting a link.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: the plan retains conforming URL-only saving.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 maker presents “hardened server-side metadata retrieval” and “app-cached icons”; Entry 6 confirms that pasting a link “fills in the details.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: automatic metadata retrieval itself is conforming. This summary does not independently establish a new preview-image scope decision beyond the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Entry 6 confirms the plan preserves the behavior that “nothing I’ve typed gets thrown away.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: preservation of user-entered metadata conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 presents the search implementation plan; Entry 6 confirms “the search understands tags.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: tag search remains conforming.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 identifies a “custom Boolean search parser”; Entry 6 confirms “and/or/not.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: the planned Boolean search behavior conforms at the recorded level.

decisions.evidence: Entry 6 confirms the presented plan retains “quoted phrases.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: exact phrase search remains conforming.

decisions.evidence: Entry 6 confirms “the tag suggestions are there” before approving the plan.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: planned tag autocomplete conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 6 confirms “favorites and my ‘still to read’ list stay separate.”
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: the unread state and its separate collection view remain conforming.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 says opening “will not mark it as read”; Entry 6 explicitly confirms that behavior before approving the plan.
decisions.note: Implementation-plan gate: manual read-state transition remains conforming.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 defines the MVP as “paste a URL … and persist the bookmark”; Entry 8 approves “the paste-a-link-and-save piece.”
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate: URL-only saving is represented by actionable work.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 includes “URL saving and automatic details” and tasks to “retrieve details safely”; Entry 8 approves “paste-and-fill saving.”
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate: the recorded automatic-details work is conforming; the summary does not state a fresh exhaustive field list.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 explicitly includes tasks to “preserve user edits”; Entry 8 approves the paste-and-fill task group.
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate: preserving editable metadata conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 includes “prevent duplicates” in the MVP. Its eventual behavior is established in Entry 10, where the client reports that a repeated URL “stopped me and pointed me back to the one I already had.”
decisions.note: Task-to-implementation decision: the initially terse duplicate task was ultimately disposed as the reference-conforming guide-to-existing behavior; it is counted once rather than as a separate pending clarification.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 includes an “Advanced search” task group; Entry 8 identifies its “search with tags” behavior before approval.
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate: tag search is represented conformingly.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 includes “Advanced search”; Entry 8 specifically confirms “and/or/not.”
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate: Boolean search is represented conformingly.

decisions.evidence: Entry 8 confirms that the search task group includes “phrases.”
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate: phrase search is represented conformingly.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 allocates a “Tag suggestions” task group; Entry 8 confirms “the tag suggestions.”
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate: autocomplete has dedicated conforming tasks.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 includes “Reading status”; Entry 8 confirms “keeping favorites separate from my read-later list.”
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate: the unread state remains distinct and conforming.

decisions.evidence: Entry 8 describes the approved behavior as a separate “read-later list.”
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate: a separate unread collection remains represented.

decisions.evidence: Entry 8 confirms the tasks preserve “opening never marking something read.”
decisions.note: Task-breakdown gate: explicit rather than automatic read-state changes remain conforming.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 presents implemented “URL-only saving”; Entry 10 reports, “saving with just a URL worked.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: URL-only saving was demonstrated and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9’s implemented metadata list is “title, description, and favicon retrieval,” again omitting preview images. Entry 10 verifies those same three fields and broadly approves the app without identifying the omitted preview image.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the delivered metadata set is narrower than REF-BM-02. The client’s approval and restatement of the three delivered fields do not explicitly surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 says fallbacks “preserve entered content”; Entry 10 verifies that “my own edits stuck.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: user metadata edits are preserved, conforming to the editable-metadata requirement.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 presents “`#tag` search”; Entry 10 verifies “I could pull up a tag with `#recipes`.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: tag-search syntax was demonstrated and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 presents “Boolean … grouped” search; Entry 10 verifies use of `NOT`.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the delivered Boolean/grouped search decision is conforming at the recorded level.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 presents “phrase” search as implemented; Entry 10 says search behaves as requested.
decisions.note: Implementation review: exact phrase support is recorded as delivered and conforming.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 presents “keyboard-accessible tag suggestions”; Entry 10 verifies, “Tag suggestions offered up what I’d already used.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: existing-tag autocomplete was demonstrated and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 presents “Independent favorites and read-later status”; Entry 10 verifies that toggling one “didn’t disturb the other.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: unread/read-later state is independently implemented and conforming.

decisions.evidence: Entry 10 verifies a distinct “‘still to read’ list” while reviewing the delivered application.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the separate unread view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 says opening links never marks them read; Entry 10 verifies a link “left it unread until I said otherwise.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: explicit marking as read conforms, with opening correctly non-mutating.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 presents “Editing”; Entry 10 reports, “Editing … worked.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the recorded bookmark-editing decision conforms at the level demonstrated.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 presents “confirmation-protected deletion”; Entry 10 reports deletion worked and “delete ask[ed] first.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: deletion conforms; confirmation is a compatible safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 presents deletion but no archive behavior. Entry 10 explicitly identifies the difference—“being able to tuck links away in an archive rather than only deleting them”—and accepts it as “a later round, not anything wrong with what you’ve delivered.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: reversible archiving distinct from deletion was absent. The client explicitly stated the missing expectation and accepted deferral.

decisions.evidence: Entry 10 identifies the absent behavior, “saving a favorite search so I can jump back to it,” and explicitly places it in “a later round” rather than rejecting the delivered version.
decisions.note: Implementation review: reusable saved searches/bundles were absent, and the client explicitly accepted that divergence for the first version.
